name: Corn
description: Corn is a vibrant, carbohydrate-rich vegetable and cereal grain. Highly regarded for its exceptional content of protective macular carotenoids like lutein and zeaxanthin, it provides a functional balance of dietary fibers and B-vitamins to sustain physical stamina and ocular health.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: A moderate-energy starchy vegetable that provides sustained, reliable fuel for muscular work and cellular respiration.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Contains a notable amount of plant proteins for a vegetable, including zein, though it should be paired with legumes for a complete amino profile.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Naturally very low in fat, containing trace heart-healthy monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids within the grain germ.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Primarily composed of complex starches and natural simple sugars, offering structured energy management to prevent rapid glucose spikes.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B1 (Thiamin)
microNutrients.description: An essential coenzyme involved in carbohydrate metabolic cascades, crucial for optimizing cognitive drive and nervous system communication.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B9 (Folate)
microNutrients.description: Vital for cellular division, nucleotide synthesis, and erythrocyte maturation, playing a protective role in cardiovascular tissue health.

microNutrients.name: Magnesium
microNutrients.description: Assists in enzymatic cellular stabilization, supporting muscular relaxation, bone health, and smooth cardiac electrical performance.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C
microNutrients.description: Provides antioxidant assistance, neutralizing surface free radicals and supporting natural immune tissue integrity.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: Mainly insoluble fibers that add mechanical volume to the stool matrix, accelerating intestinal transit and supporting digestive regularity.

microNutrients.name: Lutein
microNutrients.description: A critical antioxidant pigment that concentrates in the retinal tissues, filtering out harmful high-energy blue light and counteracting oxidative breakdown.

microNutrients.name: Zeaxanthin
microNutrients.description: Deposits directly into the central macula, working alongside lutein to safeguard visual sharpness and shield photoreceptor health.

healthBenefits: Targeted Macular Defense: The high density of lutein and zeaxanthin acts as natural "internal sunglasses," shielding retinal cells against oxidative blue light exposure and slowing macular breakdown.
Sustained Glycemic Energy: Its complex starch matrix, balanced by dietary fibers, results in steady metabolic glucose release, preventing sudden insulin crashes when eaten in whole form.
Enhanced Bowel Motility: Rich in insoluble plant fiber, corn swells within the intestinal tract, physically sweeping the colon lining, boosting peristalsis, and preventing general sluggishness.
Neuro-Metabolic Support: Substantial amounts of Thiamin (B1) support cellular energy pathways, optimizing memory mechanics and structural peripheral nerve health.
precautions: Starchy Glycemic Load Factors: Corn contains significantly more carbohydrates than leafy or watery vegetables. Individuals managing Type 2 diabetes or tracking precise glycemic parameters should control serving volumes to avoid unexpected postprandial glucose shifts.

Insoluble Outer Husk Toughness: The clear cellulose shell wrapping each individual kernel is structurally un-digestible by human stomach acid. Improperly chewed corn can pass entirely intact, causing gas, mild cramps, or bloating in sensitive digestive tracts.

Hidden Syrups & Ultra-Processed Additives: While whole sweet corn is highly therapeutic, refined commercial corn offshoots—such as High-Fructose Corn Syrup (HFCS) or processed corn starch—lack all fibers and minerals, severely aggravating metabolic liver pathways.

Fungal Mycotoxin Contamination: If stored in poorly ventilated, high-humidity corporate grain silos, corn crops can easily develop mold strains producing aflatoxins. Always consume freshly cooked or properly sealed, verified retail products.
